packet.headline_seed: 'I will never get over watching my home burn': Belfast residents reel after night of unrest
packet.description_seed: A night of disorder in Belfast saw people forced to flee their homes, in protests that followed a knife attack in the north of the city.

what: 'I will never get over watching my home burn': Belfast residents reel after night of unrest

clean_source_blocks.text: A night of disorder in Belfast saw people forced to flee their homes, in protests that followed a knife attack in the north of the city.

Families in Belfast, including one with a two-month-old baby, are counting the cost of Tuesday night's violence after being forced to flee their homes in the face of fires. A number of houses were ablaze across the city after a night of disorder amid following a knife attack on Monday night. One man, whose home of 13 years was destroyed by fire, said watching it burn down was "a feeling I'll never get over". Jamie Corrie, speaking outside the burnt out remains of his house on Lendrick Street in east Belfast, said by the time firefighters arrived his house was "already engulfed in flames". His house caught fire after a car belonging to "foreign nationals" next door was set on fire, he said.

The far right has lit the match and now they're watching my city burn. I am from North Belfast, born and bred, and watching what's been unfolding on the streets since Monday night's brutal knife attack is horrifying. Thoughts are of course foremost with the victim. We wish him and his family well after such a dreadful and traumatic incident. A 30-year-old is before the courts today and the justice system must be left to take its course. But the subsequent violence in the city and beyond cannot be justified. You could feel the tension building all day. When details emerged of what had happened and police and politicians were appealing for calm, it was clear that some people were intent on violence.

At the time of writing, the city was ablaze with violence. Thugs were roaming the streets, many covering their faces. Transport was shut down as a bus was one of dozens of vehicles set on fire. Flames were seen coming from doors and windows of terrified people's homes. There have long been outbreaks of widespread street disorder and sectarian violence in Belfast, but the anger has been redirected towards immigration. Northern Ireland is the least ethnically diverse region of the UK. Right-thinking people are horrified by more than one thing that is happening. They are appalled by Monday's knife attack and also appalled by the negative, damaging and dangerous scenes that have flowed from it. Racists, online and in person, including politicians, have been showing us all what their real agenda is.

His house caught fire after a car belonging to "foreign nationals" next door was set on fire, he said.

Corrie, who has lived on the same east Belfast street for more than a decade, said his house went up in flames.

Speaking to BBC News NI outside his home on Wednesday morning, he said he was "gutted".

"I told them before they were lighting the car, I said 'this is my property'.

"See standing there watching your house get burnt… that's a feeling I'll never get over," he says.

While he is also angry about the attack in north Belfast, he asked: "What does this resolve? What does this actually do? Burning cars out, wrecking your own community and now one of their own has just lost their home."

He said by the time firefighters arrived his house was "already engulfed in flames" and everything is destroyed.

"There's stuff in there that's sentimental, can't be replaced, that you'll not get again."

However, he's thankful his kids were not in the house at the time.

Yura, 19, is part of the Ukrainian family who were forced to flee their home on Lendrick Street in east Belfast during the disorder. She described the scenes last night as "terrifying".

"My neighbour's house was set on fire. So, my front door caught the fire a bit. It had to be kicked out to stop the fire because it was about to go in the house".

"I was with my dog at the house, so I had to escape through the back door. My neighbour's dog was trapped in the house so we were also trying to break into their house to get the dog.

"I was lucky that my friends live nearby, so they let me crash for the night."

Anselme Shima, who for 13 years has lived in east Belfast near where scenes of violence erupted on Tuesday night, said he was devastated and horrified.

"I didn't know what I can do to protect my children."

payload.title: Belfastissa asukkaita pakeni kodeistaan levottomuuksien ja tulipalojen keskeltä
payload.summary: Belfastissa useat perheet joutuivat lähtemään kodeistaan tiistai-illan väkivaltaisuuksien aikana. Levottomuudet seurasivat kaupungin pohjoisosassa maanantai-iltana tapahtunutta puukotusta.
payload.content:
Belfastissa useat asukkaat joutuivat pakenemaan kodeistaan, kun kaupungissa puhkesi tiistai-iltana väkivaltaisia levottomuuksia ja tulipaloja. Levottomuudet seurasivat maanantai-iltana Pohjois-Belfastissa tapahtunutta vakavaa puukotusta, jonka jälkeen poliitikot ja poliisi olivat vedonneet rauhallisuuteen.

## Kodit syttyivät tuleen

Tulipalot koettelivat useita perheitä eri puolilla kaupunkia. Joukossa oli myös perhe, jossa oli kahden kuukauden ikäinen vauva. Lendrick Streetillä Itä-Belfastissa asuva Jamie Corrie kertoi menettäneensä kotinsa, jossa hän oli asunut 13 vuotta.

Corrien mukaan hänen talonsa syttyi sen jälkeen, kun naapurissa ollut ulkomaalaistaustaisten henkilöiden auto oli sytytetty tuleen. Hän kuvaili talon olleen palomiesten saapuessa jo kokonaan liekkien vallassa. Kodin tuhoutumisen seuraaminen oli hänen mukaansa kokemus, josta hän ei koskaan pääse yli.

Levottomuuksien aikana liekkejä nähtiin nousevan myös asuintalojen ovista ja ikkunoista. Lisäksi liikenne häiriintyi, kun yksi linja-auto ja kymmeniä muita ajoneuvoja sytytettiin tuleen. Lähteiden mukaan kaduilla liikkui kasvojaan peittäneitä väkivaltaisia ryhmiä.

## Puukotus ei oikeuttanut väkivaltaa

Maanantai-illan puukotuksen uhri ja hänen perheensä ovat olleet tapahtumien keskiössä. Tapaukseen liittyen 30-vuotias henkilö oli määrätty oikeuden eteen, ja lähteissä korostettiin, että oikeusprosessin on annettava edetä.

Kaupungissa seurannut väkivalta on herättänyt laajaa järkytystä. Lähteissä levottomuuksia kuvataan tilanteeksi, jossa osa ihmisistä oli jo jännitteiden kasvaessa selvästi valmis väkivaltaan, vaikka viranomaiset ja poliitikot vetosivat rauhaan. Puukotusta kuvattiin vakavaksi ja traumaattiseksi tapahtumaksi, mutta sitä seurannutta väkivaltaa ei pidetty oikeutettuna.

## Viha kohdistui maahanmuuttoon

Belfastissa ja Pohjois-Irlannissa on aiemminkin nähty laajoja katulevottomuuksia ja yhteisöjen välistä väkivaltaa. Nyt vihan kuvataan kuitenkin kohdistuneen erityisesti maahanmuuttoon ja ulkomaalaistaustaisiin ihmisiin. Pohjois-Irlanti on Yhdistyneen kuningaskunnan etnisesti vähiten monimuotoinen alue.

Tapahtumat ovat jättäneet asukkaille konkreettisia menetyksiä: palaneita koteja, tuhoutuneita ajoneuvoja ja pelon siitä, voiko omaan naapurustoon enää luottaa samalla tavalla kuin ennen.
summary_bullets: Belfastissa perheitä joutui pakenemaan kodeistaan tiistai-illan levottomuuksien aikana.
Väkivalta seurasi maanantai-iltana tapahtunutta vakavaa puukotusta kaupungin pohjoisosassa.
Useita taloja ja ajoneuvoja sytytettiin tuleen, ja yksi mies kertoi menettäneensä 13 vuoden kotinsa.
